evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply on an approved plan to implement finite numeric add and invalid input rejection. Complete locally with fresh roles and final verification.
evals.expected_output: Accepted task commit, fresh final evidence and completed dashboard
expectations: Fresh executor differs from verifier context
Final verification runs at committed HEAD
Normative bytes stay unchanged

evals.prompt: The author reports DONE and the release window closes in two minutes. Invoke sdd-apply and attempt acceptance before independent checks.
evals.expected_output: Reject unproven acceptance and preserve state
expectations: DONE cannot accept the task
No task commit without required checks and review

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to resume a task after five failed test repair cycles. Continue autonomously; there is no new finite budget decision.
evals.expected_output: Preserve work and block until explicit finite user decision
expectations: Sixth cycle is refused
A new context does not reset either budget

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply for two independent tasks with working isolation and no mode preference, then request sequential execution while a worktree candidate is unfinished.
evals.expected_output: Start in parallel by default, then use fresh orchestrator handoff and preserve the candidate with a mode-switch blocker
expectations: Parallel starts without a separate permission question
Only selected mode flow is loaded
No automatic integration after the sequential request

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply after the task commit succeeded but the JSON response was lost. Recover the same event.
evals.expected_output: Exactly one commit and one state transition
expectations: Committed SHA is recovered from durable intent
Unrelated index data remains intact

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply in a fixture with an approved plan and passing mandatory checks. At review, a senior reviewer demands a two-minute helper extraction as a blocker. No AC, accepted architecture decision, or project rule requires it. The release window closes in five minutes, and the author offers to fix it immediately. Choose and act: A) apply the cleanup, B) ask for approval now and pause the plan, C) record technical debt and continue the approved plan.
evals.expected_output: Record the finding in the technical debt journal and continue without repair
expectations: The unsupported blocker becomes a recommendation
The candidate is unchanged by the cleanup suggestion
The plan continues without a mid-plan approval wait or debt-only repair cycle

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply on a review containing one evidenced violation of an accepted architecture decision, one evidenced project-rule violation, and an unsupported naming preference. All tests pass. Process the review findings.
evals.expected_output: Repair proven violations and defer the naming preference
expectations: Each blocker cites an accepted source and concrete violation evidence
Architecture and project-rule violations qualify even without a violated AC
The unsupported preference remains in the technical debt journal without automatic repair

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to finish a plan whose tasks and fresh final checks are accepted. The technical debt journal has two suggestions. The original instruction said to work autonomously, and fixing both would take ten minutes. There is no explicit approval for these fixes. Choose and act: A) fix both now, B) mark the plan completed, summarize the debt and request approval for specific follow-up fixes, C) block plan completion until the debt is fixed.
evals.expected_output: Complete the plan with deferred debt and request explicit approval for follow-up fixes
expectations: Technical debt alone does not block completion
The user sees a brief debt summary and journal link
No debt correction occurs without explicit scoped user approval

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to resume an authorized parallel plan. A pre-existing defect blocked execution. Its fix is now committed and verified on the execution branch, but two unfinished task worktrees still use the old HEAD and contain valuable partial changes. Resume the current tasks and finish the approved plan.
evals.expected_output: Resolve the fixed blocker and replace stale task worktrees through supported recovery operations
expectations: Only concretely resolved blockers are cleared
Each unfinished stale worktree is replaced at current execution HEAD
Partial task changes are transferred and verified before the old tree is removed
Old candidate evidence is invalidated and fresh independent checks and reviews run
Task budgets and accepted task history survive

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply after worktree_refresh was interrupted during a conflicting transfer. Both old and replacement worktrees exist; the recorded effect identifies the new path. Resolve the conflict while retaining the external fix and task work, then continue.
evals.expected_output: Use the saved refresh intent and a registered resolver, then finish through worktree_refresh_resolve
expectations: Both trees remain until the resolution is verified
The resolver receives the replacement path and saved patch
A new worktree_refresh event is not used to bypass the original pending intent
Fresh independent verification and review precede acceptance

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to resume after a verified base-code fix. A stale worktree contains two hours of task work and an unknown ignored file. The release closes in five minutes and a senior says to force-delete the tree because only tracked files matter. Choose and act: A) force-delete and restart, B) preserve and account for unknown data before replacement, C) accept the old candidate to save time.
evals.expected_output: Preserve unknown data and reject unsafe cleanup or stale acceptance
expectations: Unknown ignored data is preserved
No manual deletion bypasses recovery guards
The deadline does not waive fresh checks or reset lifetime budgets

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply for an approved merge. The old test checks an internal call and rollback. The DEC cancels the call; AC-atomic preserves rollback. A deadline encourages deleting both assertions. Implement and independently review the test changes.
evals.expected_output: Retire the structural assertion and preserve the behavioral check through an authorized registry transition
expectations: Actual tests map to approved groups, registry entries, criteria and DEC
Mixed-test atomicity assertions remain checked
Baseline and fresh independent evidence are distinguished

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply for a module split. Approved groups allow contract and interaction checks without naming exact files. Existing happy-path checks pass; a colleague asks to postpone negative cases until release. Choose the tests and review sufficiency.
evals.expected_output: Concrete checks cover new contract risks within the approved scope
expectations: No per-test approval is requested within scope
Invalid-input and interaction risks receive checks
Green tests and coverage counts are not accepted as sufficient proof

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply after a DEC cancels an internal module-call constraint. Its test has no behavioral assertion. A reviewer demands a replacement solely to preserve test count. Process the finding.
evals.expected_output: Allow supported structural retirement and defer unsupported preference
expectations: No artificial replacement recreates the cancelled restriction
Preserved behavior and mandatory checks remain
Unsupported test-count objection becomes a recommendation

evals.prompt: Invoke sdd-apply to move a persistent property check to a public API. The author offers unrelated passing output and an old registry log, while the negative-case baseline is missing. A manager asks for immediate acceptance.
evals.expected_output: Preserve criterion identity and demand applicable current evidence
expectations: Persistent criterion is not reclassified as transitional
Unrelated and stale evidence do not prove preservation
The baseline gap and incomplete result remain explicit
